rationale: This is essentially the archived "Maturity-Wall Investment Commitment" with the third leg swapped from debt-stock growth to net equity issuance — a cosmetic recombination of two already-tested legs (capx×equity issuance appears in at least four archived variants with near-zero alpha), and the stated "forced dilution" mechanism is not separately identified by an unconditional MIN of ranks.

The expression is internally consistent and the low-prior-leverage conditioning is a substantive sign-flip of the archived "Overlevered Debt-Funded Capex Ramp" rather than a cosmetic tweak, though the positive expected sign fights the well-documented negative base effects of both investment and debt issuance, so the burden of proof is high.

Requiring low net debt issuance plus net repurchases is largely a rediscovery of the net-share-issuance/payout anomaly, and the construction is a close cousin of the archived "Deleveraging Productive Expansion" and "Equity-Funded Deleveraging Expansion" with the financing legs simply re-signed.

The maturity-shortening-during-a-maturity-event mechanism is coherent, sign-consistent with the expression, and distinguishable from the weak archived "Short-Maturity Fixed-Investment Mismatch", but it is close to the mirror image of the already-tested "Termed-Out Investment Financing", so the informational gain is incremental.

This is the sign-flipped mirror of the archived "External Funding Excess Over Capex" (investment-minus-financing gap with an investment floor), and because the second leg is itself monotonically increasing in investment the composite is largely a repackaged investment/asset-growth measure whose natural direction opposes the stated positive expected sign.

Adding a tangibility (debt-capacity) condition to the archived "Equity-Funded Intangible Buildout" is an economically motivated refinement that sharpens the market-timing interpretation rather than a mechanical third leg, though the near-orthogonality of high PP&E intensity and rapid intangible growth risks a thin, unstable long leg.
